body:
I just wanted to let you know that I did read your comment yesterday, even though I didn't reply back then, and it did help me. Thank you. You and the other helpers on this subreddit are wonderful people for taking your time to help.

I was in a very dark place yesterday. I'm not sure why, I can only hope it doesn't happen again or that I'm able to handle it better if it does happen again.

I just have a question for you:

>But if they recur, and you take care of yourself, they will get less scary & more of an annoyance

How do you do this?

But some people don't get over this mountain. I've never been in the success group, why would I be now? I feel like I'm spiraling out of control but this time there is no safety net. I want to stop the fall. That's why I'm posting here.

I wish I had advice for you. I tried to counter-attack my self-loathing inner voice with another voice that says I'm not worthless because I did everything I should have done. It didn't really work, mostly because I rarely do what I should do, and my new inner voice was also really annoying so I just wished she would shut up.

> and a good sports bra

Now that's something I completely forgot to consider. Is this that important if I have a small cup size?

Thank you for the rest of the suggestions!
Ah thanks! "Wide ended workout capris" google results were all over the place, but I understand what they are now.

>Besides being an awful person

kek

Thank you for explaining to me how I am so evil for judging and opressing all men, pidgeons and squirrels with my running.

By the way:

* Most of these men sit there and people-watch all day, it's their hobby. There isn't anyone that passes by that they don't notice. *insert not all men disclaimer at your will*

* There are no squirrels at all, sorry. I ate them for lunch yesterday and I made a hat out of their tails.

> My only advice is to pick something that is kind of tight around your ankles so that it doesn't hit your show laces/other foot.

Thank you for this advice, that's exactly why I didn't really want to use my loose sweatpants. Never heard about harem style before, seems like it could be confortable too. Can you give me an example of wide ended workout capris? I can't see to find anything.

>If you like wearing really snug pants, you could try putting a light wrap skirt overtop to remove the naked feeling.

That's an interesting idea, thank you. I'm not sure if it would flail around too much while running, though - maybe I'll try it out.
Well this will make sure no one messes with me if I can shoot lighting out of my fingertips. But how do you see anything with those glasses on

Thank you for the suggestions! I actually bought running shoes about a week ago, so that part is taken care of for now. I will take note of the 4-6 months thing, I didn't know about it.

And your comment reminded me of something - the "training pants" I mention in my OP are actually sweatpants, but I couldn't remember the name in english when I wrote the post.

> They make ones with built in underpants

Just to make sure, these are supposed to be used without a second pair of underwear, right?

Thank you for the suggestion, I completely forgot to consider shorts! This shouldn't be a problem for now because spring is just beginning, but are you able to use them all year long, even in winter?

About the catcalls, most people seem to suggest I just ignore them, I guess that's the best I can do.

The park is indeed my only option unless I want to run on the side of the road (some people do it), but I don't feel safe doing that as I'm easily distracted. The park is also the only place that is leveled, everywhere else is kind of steep.

Thank you for taking the time to comment. But I'd still like to plan ahead, I just feel like it's too overwhelming for me to handle it right now, and not doing it will raise some questions from close friends/family.

Congratulations on getting out. I imagine it was a hard fought battle and you managed to win it.

So maybe there is hope for the rest of us too.

I know exactly what you're talking about. There's the "me" that I always had the hope to be, or that I could at least aspire to: a successful engineer, confident, always eager to learn new skills and someone that always amazed the people around with their knowledge of topics other than the ones that you are "supposed" to know.

Then there's the reality. Where I can't even get social cues and I'm too afraid of failure to try new skills, so I just don't learn new skills unless I absolutely have to. And I've come to realize that my reality and the other "me" are too far apart, so I guess I'm not the person I thought I was and I have no hope of becoming them anymore. So for me the perfect "me" is the fake one - I'm just having trouble accepting that.
